div.head: III Eg 1
div.ab: Ðis is þonne seo woruldcunde gerædnes, þe ic wille, þæt man ealde.
Ðis is þonne seo woroldcunde gerædnes, þe ic wille, þæt man healde.
Þis is ðonne seo worldcunde gerædnes, þe ic wille, þæt man healde.
Hec est institutio secularis, quam uolo per omnia teneri.
[Weoruldcund gerædnysse.] Þis is ðonne seo worldcunde gerædnes þe ic wille þæt man healde.
Ðis is þonne seo woruldcunde gerædnes þe ic wille þæt man healde.
Dies ist nun die weltliche Verordnung, die ich will, dass man halte.
This, then, is the secular ordinance which I will that men keep.
My will is further that the following be observed as a secular ordinance.
This now is the secular ordinance which I wish to be observed.
This is the secular decree that I command my subjects to obey.
div.note: D adds rubric Eadgares cynincges gerædnes

This is the secular decree: Although it is editorial convention to divide these texts into two separate pieces of legislation, no such division is indicated in the manuscripts, where 2 Edgar continues on to 3 Edgar without a break.

note.seg: h vorgesetzt G; healde So Ld
h prefixed G; healde So Ld
II Cn begins in the same way

In all the MSS there is no break between this code and the preceding one. That they were promulgated at the same meeting of the king and his councillors is apparent, as Liebermann points out, from the absence of any preamble or any mention of the king’s name, and from the use of the word þonne. A similar arrangement is found in I and II Cn. where the secular part (II Cn.) opens with almost the same formula.

note.label: gerædnysse
note.seg: The rubrics are found in Ld only.

II and III Edgar are the ecclesiastical and secular sections of a single code. It survives complete in three manuscripts. Two, C.C.C.C., MS. 201 and B.L.Harley MS. 55, are connected with Archbishop Wulfstan, and there was once a version in the part of Nero A. 1 which has entries in his hand, though this has lost all up to III Edgar 3. Readings in these manuscripts alone are suspect as due to his influence. The third complete text is in Cott. Nero A. 1, but in a part which was originally distinct from the Wulfstan part, and which is in a mid-eleventh-century hand; there is also a fragment, Bodleian MS. Vet. A 3 c. 196, a late copy of a twelfth-century manuscript, and this, like the full text in Nero A. 1, is free from the Wulfstan influence. This code is not in the post-Conquest compilations, but it is in Quadripartitus. The place of promulgation was Andover, if IV Edgar (No. 41) 1.4 refers to this code, and the date is not later than 963, the latest date for IV Edgar. The text is edited by Liebermann, I, 194–207; and with English translation by Robert son, pp. 20–9, and Thorpe, I, 262–71.
